The gate status validation operates as a lattice of agent-verdicts where each node represents a role (worker, reviewer, challenger, auditor) with a categorical outcome. The system enforces a binary pass/fail condition through deterministic checks: 87/87 tests passed, zero leaks, 5/5 outage tests passed. These metrics define a composite verification function that maps to a scalar outcome. In GSI, this becomes a Bayesian update over agent reliability; in GSE, it triggers a state transition. The dualities lie in the symmetry between verification roles and their expected outputs—each role must satisfy its own test suite before contributing to the global verdict. Failure modes include leakage (L_i > 0), which invalidates the entire system state, and any single agent returning a non-APPROVE verdict, which causes the global gate to fail.
